rows.what the ink shows: Several enclosed oval returns surround a long stem that descends and curls left; despite heavy retracing, the closed loop-and-descender structure supports varphi.
An initial short descending stroke and upper hook survive, but the horizontal cancellation runs through the following low bodies; a and r cannot be separated securely.
The raised insertion has a looped d, a detached apostrophe and two low following bodies ending in a short sloping stroke; these support d’où, though the compressed vowels limit confidence.
The first word is covered by a thick doubled horizontal cancellation. In the second, the looped d, separate i dot and later upright t remain visible, allowing directe to be recovered.
The insertion begins with a deep p-shaped return and continues through a small upright d loop to a hooked terminal t; the low connecting letters are compressed.
The subscript has a broad upper hook, a thick descending middle and a distinct rightward lower foot. That stepped outline favors 2 over the short triangular 1 in the following A subscript.

After the low initial body, an isolated middle stroke descends deeply below the writing line and the final rising run ends in a crossed t. Those features favor ayant over muni, which would require a final dotted i.
The first separate group has a narrow looped d with a long low e exit; after a clear gap, the second group shows shallow connected u/n shoulders.

The crossed first word retains a large open C and high l; the following p descends through the strike and the final q has its own lower return. The connecting bodies remain partially visible under the cancellation.

The initial l loop, apostrophe, g descender and b upright identify l’algèbre; de ses and the two p descenders of propres remain traceable. In éléments the long middle run is crossed and flattened, leaving too few separate letter bodies for a secure full recovery.

Between the quotation marks, a p descender, the small looped upright of d and the final t stem survive the horizontal strike. Their ordered positions support produit despite the flattened connecting strokes.

The separated low au and sens groups lead to looped des, then p, d and crossed t in produit. The final t has a broad return, but no separable final s can be distinguished from that return and the nearby cancellation.

The second word retains the high l, descending g loop and later b upright of algèbres. The first shows a d-like loop and short tail with a detached mark, but lacks the distinct crossed x visible in the page’s earlier deux.

The capital A has clear sloping sides and a looped lower return. Its lower-right index curls down beside a separate upper dot while cancellation crosses the join, so 1 cannot be securely distinguished from an i-like index.
